title: Auros migration harness — one run
description: Emitted once per run into <artifact_dir>/<suite_id>/<run_id>/result.json. `runner report` reads these and RECOMPUTES every verdict from the checks array; the stored `verdict` field is ignored, because a field that says 'pass' is exactly what a broken or malicious harness would write. Fails closed: a result that does not validate against this schema is counted as a FAILED run, never as an unknown or a skipped one.

host_profile.description: parallel=N reclaim_between_runs=B. Recorded because BLOCKED.md B1 is unresolved and the suite may legitimately have run serialized on a small host. The evidence is the same either way; which path produced it is not a detail worth losing.

base_system_sha256.description: The immutable Windows base image this run overlaid. Verified before AND after the run. If it ever differs between two results in a suite, the suite is not 100 runs of the same test.

corpus_digest.description: SHA-256 of golden-manifest.jsonl. Same seed produces the same corpus produces the same digest; this is the string that makes 'run 63 lost a file' reproducible.

corpus_profile.description: compact keeps all 18,000 files and every structural case but shrinks the long tail for a disk-constrained host. A suite run on compact is NOT the §6C exit condition and REPORT.md says so on its face.

pin.description: Where the fault was scheduled to fire, resolved from the golden manifest by integer arithmetic before the VM started. Present on fault runs.

fire.description: What actually happened at the pin. `fired: false` means the induced failure never occurred, which makes the run NOT EVIDENCE — a green abort suite in which nothing was ever induced is the most likely way this harness rots, and check P0 exists to catch exactly that.

overshoot_bytes.description: Observed minus pinned. Large means the installer reports progress too coarsely and the pin is nominal rather than real; it is published per run so a reader can judge that instead of trusting it.

order_violations.description: Progress lines whose file index repeated or went backwards. Non-zero means the installer is not copying in manifest order, which makes every pin in the suite meaningless.

exit_reported.description: False after a power cut, where no exit code exists and never will. A zero exit_code with exit_reported false must never be read as success.

corpus_verify.description: Every source file re-hashed against the golden manifest AFTER the run — clean or aborted, no exceptions. This is 'zero data loss' as a measurement.

allowed_deviations.description: Files a fault scenario damaged ON PURPOSE (F09/F10/F11/F12). Named explicitly so that 'zero data loss' never quietly means 'zero apart from the ones we caused and did not mention' — and so that losing TWO files in a run that should have lost one is visible.

reported.description: False means the guest never finished re-hashing. That is a failed run: an unmeasured corpus is not a verified one.

boot_check.description: REQUIRED. Spec §6C: Windows still boots normally after every abort. This is the slowest check in the suite and the one whose absence nobody notices, so it is a required property with no skip state. `performed: false` is a FAIL.

beacon_seen.description: The guest reached a usable session and said so. Its ABSENCE within the timeout is a failure, never an inconclusive.

system_state_equal.description: The first 1 MiB of PhysicalDrive0, the full BCD enumeration and the firmware boot entry, hashed. SAFETY.md phase 6 is the only code permitted to change any of it, and on an aborted run phase 6 never ran. This is 'the wall was not crossed' as a measurement rather than as the installer's own opinion.

checks.description: P0..P7. There is no 'skip' status: a check that did not run is a check that failed. Half the ways a test suite stops testing anything begin with a skip that looked reasonable.

artifacts.description: Every file the run produced, with its size and SHA-256, so REPORT.md can cite a digest per run instead of a sentence saying the run happened.

verdict.description: Written for humans. IGNORED by `runner report`, which recomputes it from the checks array.
